source_integrity.summary: Exact pending v2 and two staging locale blob SHAs pinned on current main; no public bundle exists at review.

schema_and_taxonomy.summary: Daily global macro, controlled political-economy-markets and strategic competition, English source and complete Portuguese counterpart.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Sunday Nov15 00:09 BRT cutoff; new Saturday Nov14 US aviation shutdown recovery and US–China trade negotiations; Friday Nov13 as latest US/Brazil cash closes; Japan Nov12 and Q3 GDP vintages explicit.

factual_methodology.summary: Primary DOT Nov14 ground stop 3,500 safe landings and 8,000 resumed operations; Reuters cancellations >5,300 at 16:15 ET Nov14, tariff proposals $30bn each side not enacted; AP US benchmark weekly returns 2.5/2.3/2.1/1.3%; Eurostat/ONS GDP q/q 0.4/0.5/0.7/0.8%; BLS PPI +0.3 m/m +6.5 y/y; sovereign yield 5.15 Friday. Denominators, date and stock/flow boundaries qualified.

evidence_traceability.summary: 13 identical dated evidence URLs, including US DOT, BLS, Treasury, Eurostat, ONS, ADB, BCB and IEA plus Reuters, AP and Brazilian financial press. Airline economic-loss amounts and further trade outcomes unverified and deliberately not asserted.

research_depth.summary: 3029 substantive EN words and 3317 PT-BR words, nine causal regional chapters, operational network mechanics, trade transmission, opposing explanations and economic falsifiers.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two exact equivalent numerical chart arrays (weekly US index returns and Q3 real GDP); dated quantitative evidence table, causal air-network flow, regional comparative map, four-scenario evidence matrix.

bilingual_equivalence.summary: Same 13 reference URLs and numbering in both locales, identical numeric chart series, matching cutoff and causal scenarios and non-equivalence of flight operations, tariff proposals and market returns.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: No internal publishing dialogue or article-self-reference. Natural Portuguese, direct economic mechanisms, no unsupported aggregate airline GDP loss or sensational cyber attribution.

contrary_evidence.summary: Weekend flights did not return to normal immediately, Friday equity losses alongside weekly gains, tariffs not enacted, GDP estimates not equal to jobs and dollar financing impacts vary by borrower.

counterfactual_review.summary: Transient versus systemic aviation fault; tariff negotiation versus execution; producer costs versus consumer inflation; credit conditions versus sovereign yields, each with observational tests.

pipeline_validation.summary: Source grammar and quantitative/depth gates inspected directly; npm production build, index/ledger reconciliation and live HTTP smoke tests reserved to publisher and CI.

contrary_evidence: Positive US weekly equity returns coexist with negative Friday cash-market closes.
Open US airspace does not imply that displaced airline networks have returned to normal.
A negotiated tariff figure does not prove enacted concessions or realized imports.
Producer-price inflation and sovereign yields do not map one for one onto CPI or corporate borrowing rates.
limitations: 14 November cancellation counts are time-bound operational observations, not final financial or GDP loss.
US-China tariff measures remain under negotiation, with no ratified cuts treated as completed.
Japanese bond/currency data refer to 12 November and Friday equities/yields to 13 November.
No verified total for affected Brazil-US travelers or global private credit spreads.
Editorial automated review is assistant-led and not independent human peer review; deployment must be checked separately.
notes: SHA-pinned v2 approval for 15 November Sunday Global Macro; evidence checked against current dated official and media sources, with cutoff and uncertainty preserved.
